description: Figure 5 presents a diagram illustrating the results of Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) under three different expansion settings—corpus expansion, document expansion, and asymmetric expansion—evaluated on the development set of the MS-Marco dataset. The diagram is structured into three horizontal sections, each corresponding to one expansion method. In the top section, labeled “Document Expansion,” a query q is shown being used to retrieve a target document d_i, alongside S additional query expansions q_i^1 through q_i^S, which are depicted as pink circles. The middle section, labeled “Corpus Expansion,” shows the same query q retrieving the same target document d_i, but with the additional queries q_i^1 through q_i^S shown as pink circles arranged vertically below the document. The bottom section, labeled “Relevance to query q,” displays the S queries ranked by relevance to the original query q, with the most relevant query q_i^1 shown first, followed by q_i^2, and so on, decreasing in relevance, indicated by a descending arrow and the notation q_i^1 > q_i^2 > ... > q_i^S. The diagram visually contrasts how each expansion method treats the additional queries during retrieval, with document expansion including them alongside the target document, corpus expansion treating them as separate retrieval targets, and the relevance section indicating the relative importance of each query.
